  • from the centre of rotation. In short, particles in suspe nsion experience a

questions.question: What is radioimmunoassay? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What is radioimmunoassay? [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: Radioimmunoassay (RIA) is a technique used to measure the
  • concentration of an antigen, such as a hormone in a sample . It works by using a
  • radioactive-labeled antigen and a specific antibody to compete for binding with
  • the unlabeled antigen from the sample. The more unlabeled antigen is in the
  • sample, the less radioactive-labeled antigen binds, allowing for a quantifiable
  • measurement of the unknown sample's antigen concentration.

questions.question: Explain the major parts of a spectrophotometer and illustrate them with a diagram. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the major parts of a spectrophotometer and illustrate them with a
  • diagram. [U] / [CO2]
  • Ans; -
  • INSTRUMENTATION
  • The general instrument set up for any spectrophotometry requires;
  • • Radiation source - It can be of Argon, Xenon lamb , Nernst glower etc..
  • • Condensing lens – Inorder to generate a parallel beam of light.
  • • Monochromator - to break the polychromatic radiation into component
  • wavelength (or) bands of wavelengths.
  • • Wavelength selection (slit) – It can be achieved by absorption filters ,or by
  • inference filters. Fused silica or quartz prism is used in UV regions
  • • Sample holder – Type of sample holder depends on the transmission range
  • of the materials. Generally glass is used in UV regions (300-500nm)
  • • Photosensitive detector and an associated readout system -Detectors
  • generate electronic signals which are proportional to the transmitter light.

questions.question: Why is the glass electrode selective to hydrogen ions? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is the glass electrode selective to hydrogen ions? [U] / [CO2]
  • Ans; -
  • • The glass electrode is selective to hydrogen ions because its special glass
  • membrane develops a potential difference when it interacts with the
  • solution.
  • • This selectivity comes from the ability of hydrogen ions to exchange with
  • a very thin, hydrated gel layer on the glass's surface, displacing other ions.
  • • The resulting potential difference is a direct function of the H + ion
  • concentration
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a note on isoelectric focusing and its importance in protein characterization. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on isoelectric focusing and its importance in protein
  • characterization. [U] / [CO2, CO3]
  • Ans;-
  • Isoelectric focusing (IEF) is a powerful analytical technique used primarily for
  • the separation of proteins and other biomolecules based on their isoelectric
  • points (pI). The isoelectric point of a protein is the pH at which the molecule
  • carries no net electrical charge . IEF operates on the principle that proteins will
  • migrate in an electric field until they reach a point in a pH gradient where their
  • net charge is zero—this point is their isoelectric point

questions.question: Which analytical method you would prefer to seperate the individual components of a mixture? / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Which analytical method you would prefer to separate the individual
  • components of a mixture? [U] / [CO2, CO3]
  • Ans;-
  • ● Chromatography can be used to separate the individual components of a
  • mixture
  • ● Chromatography is an important biophysical technique that enables the
  • separation, identification, and purification of the components of a mixture
  • for qualitative and quantitative analysis.
  • ● Proteins can be purified based on characteristics such as size and shape,
  • total charge, hydrophobic groups present on the surface, and binding
  • capacity with the stationary phase.
  • ● Four separation techniques based on molecular characteristics and
  • interaction type use mechanisms of ion exchange, surface adsorption,
  • partition, and size exclusion.
